reviews.title: Money siphoning scheme
reviews.text:
After syncing my LinkedIn I was accepted within 12 hours. However upon using the app it was filled with money making scheme with the lowest 1 week upgrade price starting from £60/week. Everything required payment from seeing individuals who liked you to setting up basic filter only 2 filters are free- location and age range but every time you go to the homepage the filter resets. 

Then there is the issue of the “curated” options that only refreshes after 24 hours but the curated options does not take your preferred age range into account which is quite silly imo. 

I think the creators really need to review the price plan and app layout because if all the users are expressing that its too expensive maybe it’s time to focus on meeting the customer demands rather than solely profiting off people looking for a genuine interaction.

reviews.title: Broken Buggy Mess (Possible Scam)
reviews.text:
Filled out the application.

They require some unusual form of verification: linking LinkedIn, a school email, a work email or access to some weird doctor's portal. If you don't have that you're SOL and they "encourage" you to instead pay for access.

Even if you fill out the application fully, the app tells you your application is only 51-52% completed and insist you complete it.

They provide you with a "concierge" which claims to be a real person with degrees and work experience but is actually ChatGPT wearing likely some user's profile picture as a skin suit.

I contacted support about not being able/willing to provide these weird verification methods (as if I'm giving an unverified service my work email are you joking?). They claimed to be able to fill out the rest of my application if I provided it to them in a reply to the email. I did and my application never got updated.

At some point the AI bot told me my application was accepted and then quickly rescinded it.

I again reached out to support but this time I got nothing. I reached out repeatedly and got nothing.

All things considered, the opaque waitlist, the AI skinwalker, the unhelpful support, the broken buggy mess, I have strong reason to believe that this service is a scam.

reviews.title: Over promise, under deliver
reviews.text:
Few matches - I have had this app for about five months. In that time, there were weeks I used it daily. I had fewer than 10 matches and never went on a single date from this app. 

Low quality profiles - I have a law degree. I was interested in this app because I hoped to mostly see profiles of people with at least a bachelors degree, and perhaps people more advanced in their career.  On the free version of the app, you only get to swipe on 3 to 5 profiles a day. I don’t hate this on its own, but the algorithm felt pretty weak as far as the potential matches it gave me daily. In my batch of four profiles for today, there was one person with a trade school background and one person with an associates degree from community college. Nothing wrong with that, but not really the professionals dating professionals vibe that this app promises in its advertising.

Can’t update profile - I created my account shortly after graduating law school, But because I had not yet been admitted to the bar, I didn’t label myself as an attorney. I went to update my account, and was told I could not update my profession from “Law clerk” to “Attorney” on the free version of the app. I even contacted customer support to ask them to change it, but they declined based on my free user status. For an app that advertises dating based on professional credentials, you’d think they would want you to have accurate ones on there! 

This was the straw that broke me; I am deleting this app and leaving this revie

reviews.title: Worse app I ever tried
reviews.text:
One of the worst dating app experiences I’ve had.
The League presents itself as an exclusive platform with high-quality profiles, but my experience was very different. Interaction was extremely limited, I had very few meaningful conversations, and I never actually met anyone in person through the app.

More seriously, one of the people I connected with through the app eventually tried to get money from me under circumstances that raised major scam concerns. That experience alone significantly damaged my trust in the platform and in how effectively profiles are being screened or monitored.

I also came across profiles whose photos appeared AI-generated or heavily manipulated, which created additional concerns about authenticity.

On top of that, the free version is extremely restrictive and repeatedly pushes users toward paid access. For an app positioned as selective and premium, I expected much stronger safeguards, transparency, and genuine interaction.

I’m deleting the app and would not use it again.

I’ve also encountered many men who list one age and then admit in their profile that they’re actually a different age. Some profiles are looking for casual dating, threesomes, or other arrangements that I wouldn’t expect to see so frequently on a service marketed as selective and premium.

If the preferences are only suggestions rather than meaningful filters, I think that should be made much clearer before people pay for a membership.

I’ve also run across some fake AI account accounts as well.

reviews.title: A Lifestyle Feed With extra Fees
reviews.text:
The League charges you to join, then keeps charging you to actually use the dating features.

You can pay for a membership and still be asked to pay again to see who liked you, who messaged you, and to get more access to swiping. So what exactly did the first payment unlock?

Meanwhile, a large part of the experience is just browsing highly curated profiles full of careers, vacations, restaurants, bars, hotels and lifestyle highlights.

That content is not premium. You can see people showing off their lifestyle for free on Instagram.

A dating app should be selling access to better connections, not charging you repeatedly to look at someone’s travel history, dinner photos and professional résumé.

And paying more does not suddenly create better conversations or more meaningful dating. It simply gives you more access to the same type of profiles and the same limited interaction.

If I wanted to pay to watch people showcase their lifestyle, I wouldn’t need a dating app. Social media already does that for free.

The League markets exclusivity, but the actual experience feels like multiple paywalls wrapped around a lifestyle feed.

reviews.title: Mrs
reviews.text:
I paid for League Select and then paid separately for a Boost. After paying, I discovered that I still cannot see the people who have liked me, and I cannot properly control the age range I am shown without paying for yet another upgrade.

I am currently being shown men aged 35–41, which is completely irrelevant to me. I am looking for a partner in my own age range, not someone young enough to feel like I need to adopt him.

The Boost simply increases your visibility, but the likes it generates remain hidden unless you pay again. The whole pricing structure feels extremely aggressive: you pay for Select, then Boost, then discover that useful features are still locked behind Premium, Unlimited and ultimately an Omni tier costing around £5,000 for three months.

For that kind of pricing, I expected a genuinely premium dating experience, not a series of paywalls around basic functionality. I cancelled auto-renewal almost immediately.

I do not recommend it.

reviews.title: Nearly $100 a Month for a Very Limited Experience
reviews.text:
I really wanted to give The League a fair chance, which is why I was willing to pay nearly $100 for a one-month subscription. Unfortunately, even in the short time I’ve been using the paid version, I’m extremely disappointed and genuinely confused about what I’m paying for.

For that price, I expected significantly more access and a dating experience tailored to the preferences I selected. Instead, I’m given a small batch of approximately 4–6 profiles at a time, and many of those profiles don’t even meet the preferences I’ve set. I’ve been shown people outside of my preferred age range and people whose relationship goals don’t align with what I’m looking for. Some aren’t looking for marriage or intentional dating at all.

After going through a batch, I’m then expected to wait hours—sometimes until the next day—for another small batch. So I’m paying nearly $100 a month, yet I can’t freely browse a larger pool of potential matches, and when the app finally does provide another batch, I’m still being shown people who don’t meet my basic preferences.

What makes this even more frustrating is how limited the preference settings are at this subscription level. So far, I’m primarily able to control things like age and distance. For an app that markets itself as a more selective dating experience, I expected much more detailed compatibility filtering—especially for paying members.

reviews.title: Money grab, zero stars
reviews.text:
What a joke. They brag about their “application” process and how it’s highly selective. Any idiot can create a linked in profile and have it say what they want. There’s a “wait list,” and yet unsurprisingly it took an hour for my application to be approved. It’s “curated,” and yet every single batch of profiles I’ve been shown have things outside of my selected preferences. My preferences were people over age 38 who live within 10 miles of downtown with an education level above undergrad, and I was shown a 34 year old farmer out in the sticks. If you’re only gonna let me look at 3-5 profiles a day, at least make them aligned with my preferences. Unlike Bumble where you really only pay to view “likes” and “boost” your profile, this app prompts you to pay for everything, including just looking at profiles outside of your daily batch and even paying to see if your chat message has been “read” by the other person. You pay to restrict your preferences by age to tighter than 10 years. You pay to edit your job description. You pay to hide your marriage preference. Every time I click something there’s a new box popping up to ask if I want to pay. 
This app is going in the “delete” pile.

reviews.title: Frustrating Experience with Settings and Matches
reviews.text:
I’ve been using this app for about two weeks now, and honestly, the experience has been quite underwhelming so far. One of the most frustrating issues is with the age preferences—I’ve repeatedly updated my preferred age range, but every time I exit and reopen the app, it resets and starts again from 24. Because of this, the profiles being shown to me are mostly 30 and below, which doesn’t align with what I’m actually looking for. It makes the matching process feel misaligned and inconsistent from the start.

In terms of engagement, I’ve only received one like in these two weeks. While I understand that this app promotes a slower, more intentional dating approach, the level of activity feels too low. On other apps, I typically receive at least 3–4 likes a day, which makes the experience feel more dynamic and encouraging.

I appreciate the idea of mindful or slow dating, but I do think there needs to be a better balance. Even with a slower pace, having at least one like a day or more relevant matches would make the app feel more engaging and worth investing time in.

Overall, it has potential, but the matching algorithm, settings stability, and activity levels could definitely be improved.

reviews.title: Exclusive spelled “expensive”
reviews.text:
I wanted to like The League, but it feels more like manufactured exclusivity than anything real. The whole premise is that it’s selective and higher quality, but in practice the dating pool is small and not noticeably better than other apps.
It’s also not from lack of matches on my end. I used the app for a week, went through my daily “batch,” and almost every profile was a no. I eventually matched with a couple people, but those matches were completely unresponsive, which defeats the whole point.
The pricing structure is where it really loses me. It’s already expensive, but the experience still feels locked behind even higher tiers. Like you don’t actually get full functionality unless you’re paying hundreds per month. Even basic interaction feels restricted. I’d get messages from the “concierge,” but when I asked questions, I’d either get no response or an automated reply that basically implied I needed to pay more to get real support.
At that point, it just feels like you’re paying for access to features that should already be included. Honestly, Facebook Dating is probably a better place to meet someone, and it’s free.
Overall, this feels like a premium price for branding, not results.

reviews.title: Algorithm ignores preferences
reviews.text:
I want to love this app, I really do. I love the format — 3-5 potential matches daily. This is great because you don’t get overwhelmed with matches that you never talk to. 

Unfortunately, I can only give it two stars. I have distance as my most important preference, being within 50 miles. I’m a gay male living in metro Detroit. There are plenty of gay men in my area. The app consistently shows me people who are 3+ hours away. And that’s on the closer end. They’re mostly in New York or Virginia oddly enough. Meanwhile it shows me three profiles in the search feature that are all local and people I’d be very interested in trying to match with. However, I’m unable to interact with those profiles because I am on the free version. I considered paying, but I’m hesitant due to the steep price point and the fact that it does not give me any quality matches on the free version so I don’t want to pay for a premium version and be left in the same situation. 

The developers really need to look into their algorithm for matching people as I do not think it is working. Or, it’s working perfect as designed and the design is to force people to pay to actually have a chance of actually meeting someone. 

I’m aware you have to be profitable and don’t mind paying if the service actually delivers the desired results, but I’m not confident that it will.
